items.text: Fourteen Wednesdays — the soil of the heart, our stories, confession and restoration, hearing God in scripture, the gardens of our hearts, the quiet doubts, what was prepared for us
Tonight is the integration. The four Connects are not separate disciplines — they are a sequence: Self, Others, God, Mission. Each one creates the conditions for the next.
They are also a way of life — lived in family, witnessed in community
Tonight: each parent-and-teen pair stands in the center; each speaks a specific witnessed blessing over the other; the whole community speaks the Aaronic blessing over each family
If you are new tonight: your job is to bear witness. Your presence is the gift.
Three sentences. Just three. The worksheet you got Friday — H21.1 — has the form.
“What I have specifically seen God doing in you across Getting Started is _____.” Something you actually noticed.
“What I bless in you tonight is _____.” Something true about who they are.
“What I commit to you in our relationship moving forward is _____.” Something you will actually do.
The brevity is the discipline — we are not making speeches; we are speaking truth in front of witnesses
Two Companions demo a real blessing, then brief questions
Two scriptures before we begin — the blessing itself, and what we are commissioning each other into
The Aaronic blessing is not a generic prayer — it is the specific words God gave Aaron and his sons to speak over Israel. When we speak it over each other, we are not improvising.
Philippians 1:6 — Getting Started is not the completion; it is part of the beginning. The next stretch is a longer work that is His to finish, not ours.
“And I am sure of this, that he who began a good work in you will bring it to completion at the day of Jesus Christ.” — Philippians 1:6
Then prayer over the commissioning to come

panel.label: NUMBERS 6:24–26
lines: “The Lord bless you and keep you;
the Lord make his face to shine upon you and be gracious to you;
the Lord lift up his countenance upon you and give you peace.”

items.text: Each family in turn — parent and teen stand in the center; the rest of the family stands behind them in support
Brief framing — “We have walked with [name] through Getting Started; we have seen _____.”
Teen blesses parent first — the three sentences
Parent blesses teen — the three sentences
“Family of [last name], the community now blesses you.” The whole room speaks the Aaronic blessing aloud together, slowly.
If you freeze — take your time, or ask the other person to read your worksheet for you. If you cry, that is fine. The room can wait.
Around the circle, each person: one specific takeaway from Getting Started, and one specific next commitment — about thirty seconds each
The takeaway can be small — “I learned that I can name a doubt without losing my faith.” “I learned that my dad sees me.”
The commitment can be small too — “I will keep the morning question.” “I will tell my mom one true thing this week.”
You can pass. Visiting family can pass — or share if you want to. The Cluster Companions go first; a parent opens for the families.

slides.title: Rhythm Card and Going Deeper Bridge

items.text: The Daily / Weekly / Monthly Rhythm Card (H21.3) — daily: the morning question and an evening journal note; weekly: one person who knows what you are working on; monthly: a clearing time. It is your card, in your handwriting.
The Going Deeper bridge (H21.4) — twelve Wednesdays. Decide on your own time. Tonight is not a recruiting pitch.
The Post-Series Survey — the bin at the door tonight, or email it this week. The next group of families benefits from your honesty.
If a daily practice slips — do not start over from scratch; start the next day. Streaks are not the point. Returning is the point.
